conclusion: **Curation did not beat random selection on classifier performance.** On the eight datasets where it could be evaluated (three canonical, five new), quality-coverage minus admitted-random differences were small and mixed in sign (median F1 difference +0.001 for logistic regression and +0.013 for random forest; exploratory Wilcoxon p between 0.19 and 1.00 for F1 and AP). Its geometric benefit did hold up: on all five new datasets with usable pools, quality-coverage covered more of the training data with fewer near-duplicates than random selection from the same admitted pool (for example 0.677 vs 0.461 coverage on abalone9-18), and on the historical pools it also covered more than equal-budget random subsets of B2-accepted records. Setting the minority quota to the real class ratio left coverage unchanged, raised pure synthetic-only F1 on page-blocks0 but lowered it on Ecoli4 and Abalone19, and barely moved hybrid results, while the equal-budget B2 control was neither consistently better nor worse than quality-coverage. These results are exploratory: several datasets have only 4-10 positive test records per split, vehicle0's unrounded SMOTE candidates were all structurally non-compliant (bounded repair rescued 6 of 1,400), winequality-red-4 could not be obtained, and the occasional advantage of the best augmentation over real-only training is selected on the same test splits and is therefore optimistic.
